decisions.reason: Separate payouts and payment processing were already required for each location; the source reaffirms rather than changes that state.
The source's Seattle-template clause is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the business-data isolation updates require no additional template-state change.
The source's booking activation and coming-soon effects are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; separate booking data is owned by the source Requirement.
The source's coming-soon mode, layout, button, and opening transition are already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE.
The VIP signup and Join VIP List button are already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE; backend data isolation adds no further signup change.
Keeping Seattle operationally independent does not alter the master site's existing national branding and aggregation role.
The candidate already requires separate Wix websites and accounts for operational locations, including Seattle; the source reaffirms that architecture without changing it.
Backend operational isolation does not change the established visual design references or cross-location branding consistency.
The source specifies Seattle location-page content, not changes to the master homepage section composition.
The candidate already requires a dedicated Seattle experience with consistent branding; backend independence does not change that frontend model.
The source does not change the location selector, available location options, or routing destination.
Location business-data isolation has no necessary effect on the site's mobile-friendly responsive behavior.
